tools.description:
Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

If you already know a concrete file path and need to inspect its contents, use Read directly instead.

Write patterns in ripgrep regex syntax, which differs from POSIX `grep` syntax. For example, braces are special, so escape them as `\{` to match a literal `{`.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always skipped for safety, even when `include_ignored` is `true`.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing — use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. Defaults to `files_with_matches`.

-i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Read a text file from the local filesystem.

If the user provides a concrete file path to a text file, call Read directly. Do not `Glob`, `ls`, or otherwise pre-check known text file paths; missing or invalid file paths return errors you can handle. Do not use Read for directories; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob when you need files matching a name pattern (Glob lists files only, never directories). Use `Grep` only when the task is to search for unknown content or locations.

When you need several files, prefer to read them in parallel: emit multiple `Read` calls in a single response instead of reading one file per turn.

- Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.
- Returns up to 1000 lines or 100 KB per call, whichever comes first; lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated mid-line.
- Page larger files with `line_offset` (1-based start line) and `n_lines`. Omit `n_lines` to read up to the 1000-line cap.
- Sensitive files (`.env` files, credential stores, SSH private keys, and similar secrets) are refused to protect secrets; do not attempt to read them. Templates and public keys are exempt: `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` and public SSH keys such as `id_rsa.pub` read normally.
- Only UTF-8 text files can be read. Non-UTF-8 encodings, binary files, and files containing NUL bytes are refused; use `ReadMediaFile` for images or video, and Bash or an MCP tool for other binary formats.
- Negative line_offset reads from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines); the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.
- Output format: `<line-number>\t<content>` per line.
- A `<system>...</system>` status block is appended after the file content; it summarizes how much was read (line and byte counts, truncation, line-ending notes) and is not part of the file itself.
- Pure CRLF files are displayed with LF line endings; `Edit` matches this output and preserves CRLF when writing back.
- Mixed or lone carriage-return line endings are shown as `\r` and require exact `Edit.old_string` escapes.
- After a successful `Edit`/`Write`, do not re-read solely to prove the write landed. When the task depends on an exact file, API, or output shape, inspect the final external contract before finishing.

path.description: Path to a text file. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories are not supported; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob for pattern search.

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Omit to start at line 1. Negative values read from the end of the file; the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.

n_lines.description: The number of lines to read; the tool also applies its internal cap. Omit to read up to the internal cap of 1000 lines.

# lnav 0.14.0 headless colon-command behavioral spec

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`lnav 0.14.0-07efb63`).
All tests run as: `/workspace/executable -n -N [-q] -c '<cmd>' ... [file]` from `/tmp/t/cmds`.
Test files: `test.log` (8 timestamped lines, levels INFO/DEBUG/WARN/ERROR, 2024-01-15T10:00:01–08)
and `plain.txt` (5 plain text lines). `cat -A` notation: `$` = end-of-line, `M-b...` = UTF-8 bytes.

## 0. Global headless behavior (critical context)

- When stdout is NOT a TTY and no `-q` is given, lnav dumps the **top view** to stdout at
  exit: all visible (post-filter) lines from the current top-of-view line to the end.
  - After a `;SELECT`, the top view is the DB result, dumped as plain aligned columns
    (see §5 write-screen-to format), NOT the boxed table.
  - After `:sh`, top view = captured command output.
  - The dump is **suppressed** if any `-c` command already wrote to stdout
    (`:echo`, `:write-*-to -`, `:sh`, ...). Verified: `-c ':goto 3' -c ':echo hi' test.log`
    prints only `hi`.
- `-q` suppresses this exit dump entirely. `-q` does NOT suppress `:echo` output.
- Errors during `-c` execution go to **stderr**; exit code stays **0**. Subsequent `-c`
  commands still run after an error.
- Exit code **1** observed only when a file given as a CLI argument cannot be opened:
  stderr:
  ```
    error: unable to open file: /nonexistent/file.log
   reason: No such file or directory
  ```
  (`:open /nonexistent2.log` from `-c` gives `error: cannot open file: ...` + reason, exit 0.)
- Multiple `-c` options execute in order; each `:echo` output appears in order.
- `-c` args starting with `;` run SQL; starting with `:` run commands. SQL errors:
  ```
    error: failed to compile SQL statement
   reason: no such table: nosuch_table
   --> command-option:1
   | SELECT * FROM nosuch_table              
  ```
  (also `reason: near "here": syntax error` for bad syntax). Exit still 0.

## 1. Error message formats (all on stderr, exit 0)

### Unknown command (single line, no source box):
```
  error: unknown command: ‘nosuchcmd’
```
Quotes are U+2018/U+2019 (`‘’`, bytes e2 80 98 / e2 80 99). If similar commands exist,
appended (e.g. for `:head`):
```
 = note: did you mean one of the following:
           clear-all-sticky-headers - Clear all sticky header bookmarks in the current view
           hide-unmarked-lines - Hide lines that have not been bookmarked
           show-lines-before-and-after - Show lines that were hidden by the 'hide-lines' commands
           toggle-sticky-header - Toggle the sticky header state for the focused line in the current view
```
(`:echoln`, `:pwd`, `:tail` → plain unknown-command error with no note.)

### Command argument errors (multi-line box), e.g. `:filter-in` with no arg:
```
  error: expecting a regular expression to filter
 --> command-option:1
 | :filter-in                              
 = help: :filter-in pattern
         ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
           Only show lines that match the given regular expression in the
           current view
```
- `command-option:N` = 1-based index of the failing `-c` option on the command line.
- ` | ` + the original command text, right-padded with spaces to (at least) 43 columns.
- ` = help: ` + command signature line, then 8 spaces + 71 `═` (U+2550) chars,
  then 10-space-indented short description of the command (wrapped at ~70 cols).
- No trailing blank line; message ends with newline.

### Bad regex, e.g. `:filter-in [` or `:highlight [`:
```
  error: ‘[’ is not a valid regular expression
 reason: missing terminating ] for character class
 --> pattern
 | [                                           
 |  ^ missing terminating ] for character class
 = help: :filter-in pattern
         ═══...═══
           <command description>
```
- ` | ` + pattern and ` |  ^ <pcre error>` lines both right-padded to the width of the
  longest line in that block (here 47 columns total).
- `:delete-filter nosuchfilter` → single line: `  error: unknown filter -- nosuchfilter`
- `:disable-filter ERROR` (no such filter) → `  error: no such filter -- ERROR`

### Other captured single-line/simple errors:
- `:eval` (no arg): box with `  error: expecting a command or query to evaluate`
- `:unix-time` (no arg): box with `  error: expecting a unix time value`
- `:comment` (no arg): box with `  error: expecting some comment text`
- `:tag` (no arg): `  error: expecting one or more tags` (single line)
- `:annotate` (no annotations): box with `  error: no annotations available for this log message`
- `:cd /nonexistent-dir`: box with `  error: cannot access -- /nonexistent-dir` +
  ` reason: No such file or directory`
- `:redirect-to /nonexistent-dir/x.txt`: box with `  error: unable to open file -- /nonexistent-dir/x.txt`
- `:write-to` / `:write-raw-to` with no marked lines: box with
  `  error: no lines marked to write, use 'm' to mark lines`
- `:write-jsonlines-to` in TEXT view: box with
  `  error: write-jsonlines-to is only supported for the LOG and DB views`
- `:goto abc`: box with `  error: invalid argument: abc` +
  ` reason: expecting line number/percentage, timestamp, or relative time`
- `:convert-time-to UTC`: single line (this env lacks zoneinfo):
  `  error: Unable to get timezone: UTC -- discover_tz_dir failed to find zoneinfo`

## 2. :echo [-n] msg

Output goes to **stdout** (or to the `:redirect-to` file). Exit 0.

- The message is everything after `:echo ` (exactly one separating space consumed);
  the rest is VERBATIM: leading/trailing/multiple spaces preserved
  (`:echo a  b   c` → `a  b   c`; `:echo    spaced out   ` → `   spaced out   `).
- Quotes are NOT stripped: `:echo "double" 'single' mixed` → `"double" 'single' mixed`.
- `:echo` with no message → prints just `\n`.
- `-n` flag suppresses the trailing newline (`:echo -n no newline here` → no `\n`).
  Consecutive `-n` echos concatenate: `-n a` + `-n b` + `c` → `abc\n`.
- Environment variable substitution IS performed: `$HOME` and `${HOME}` expand;
  undefined vars expand to empty (`undefined $NOSUCHVAR end` → `undefined  end`;
  `$1 $2` → ` `). `$(HOME)` → `(HOME)` (a `$` before a non-var char is dropped).
- Backslash escapes the next char (prevents substitution): `\$HOME` → `$HOME`.
  `\t`, `\n` are NOT escape sequences: `tab\there` → `tabthere`, `newline\nhere` →
  `newlinenhere`; literal `\\` → `\`.
- `%s %d` pass through unformatted. `;` in message is fine (`; semicolon test` printed).
- `:eval :echo hello from eval` works — echo output via eval also goes to stdout.

## 3. :eval command

"Evaluate the given command/query after doing environment variable substitution".
- `:eval ;SELECT 1+1` → runs the SQL, result visible (table `   1+1     \n         2 \n`
  on stdout as the exit dump).
- `:eval :echo hello from eval` → `hello from eval`.
- `:eval 1+1` / `:eval 'str'` → treated as lnav command →
  `error: unknown command: ‘1+1’` WITH the full `= help: :eval command` box.
- `:eval` alone → `error: expecting a command or query to evaluate` + help box.
- Env vars substituted before execution: `:eval :echo HOME is $HOME` →
  `HOME is /opt/uiuc-agent/home`.

## 4. :filter-in / :filter-out (and related)

- Affect which lines appear in the exit dump / `:write-*` view output.
- `:filter-in ERROR` → only the 2 ERROR lines dumped. `:filter-out ERROR` → other 6.
- Multiple filters combine (AND): filter-in ERROR + filter-out timeout → 1 line.
- Adding the same filter twice: silently idempotent, no error.
- With no file loaded: no output, no error, exit 0.
- Non-matching filter → empty dump (no output at all).
- `:delete-filter <unknown>` → `error: unknown filter -- <pattern>`;
  `:disable-filter <unknown>` → `error: no such filter -- <pattern>`.
- `:filter-expr :log_level = 'error'` works (SQL expr with `:col` refs), same 2 lines.
- `:hide-lines-before 2024-01-15T10:00:04` → dump starts at that timestamp (inclusive).
- `:hide-lines-after 2024-01-15T10:00:04` → dump ends at that timestamp (inclusive).
- `:set-min-log-level error` → only ERROR lines. Invalid level (`bogus`) silently
  ignored — no error, all lines shown.
- `:goto 0` + `:mark` + `:hide-unmarked-lines` → only marked line dumped.

## 5. :write-* family

Common: `path` of `-` writes to stdout (and suppresses the exit dump). Writing to a
real file produces **no confirmation message** (no "wrote N rows") on stdout/stderr in
headless mode. Existing files are silently overwritten (`:write-to`). No `-q` effect on
the file contents. `--anonymize` replaces words with dictionary words
(sample: `2024-... INFO abaft up abashed aberrant`, leading space added, level words
anonymized for DEBUG/ERROR but timestamps/numbers/`user bob`/`id=42` partly preserved).

- `:write-to PATH` — marked lines only, raw content. No marks → error box
  `no lines marked to write, use 'm' to mark lines`. Use `:mark-expr 1` to mark all.
- `:write-raw-to [--view log|db] PATH` — same "no lines marked" requirement in log view;
  in DB view writes raw cell contents (`SELECT 1` → file/stdout content `1\n`).
- `:write-jsonlines-to [--all] PATH` — `--all` = all visible lines (no marks needed).
  One compact JSON object per line, e.g.:
  `{"log_path":"/tmp/t/cmds/test.log","log_time":"2024-01-15T10:00:01.000000","log_level":"info","log_line_link":"#msg00060ef913bc0a40-v1:3284a5bdc002d898c8b94510a62ff26c","log_time":"2024-01-15T10:00:01.000","log_level":"INFO"}`
  (note: format fields appear twice — normalized + original from the log format).
  For SQL results: `{"one":1,"two":2.5,"three":"three"}`.
  TEXT view → error `only supported for the LOG and DB views`.
- `:write-csv-to PATH` — SQL results as CSV with header row: `one,two,three\n1,2.5,three\n`.
- `:write-json-to PATH` — SQL results, 4-space-indented array of objects:
  ```
  [
      {
          "one": 1,
          "two": 2.5,
          "three": "three"
      }
  ]
  ```
- `:write-json-cols-to PATH` — column-oriented; unusual leading-comma style:
  ```
  [
      {"name":"one","type":"integer","width":10,"values":[1]}
      ,{"name":"two","type":"integer","width":10,"values":[2]}
      ]
  ```
- `:write-table-to PATH` — Unicode box table WITH ANSI bold header (`\e[1m...\e[0m`),
  even when writing to a plain file or pipe:
  ```
  ┌───────────┬───────────┬─────┐
  │   one     │   two     │three│
  ├───────────┼───────────┼─────┤
  │         1│       2.5│three│
  └───────────┴───────────┴─────┘
  ```
  (numeric columns right-aligned, text left-aligned; column content width 10 here.)
- `:write-screen-to PATH` — plain aligned columns, no ANSI; same as the exit-dump
  format for the DB view:
  ```
     one        two     three $
           1        2.5 three $
  ```
  (each column 10 wide, right-aligned numbers, trailing space at line end).
  In the log/text view it writes the displayed log lines (respects filters).
- `:write-view-to PATH` — like write-screen-to for the log view (all visible lines,
  respects filters). Difference vs screen: view = whole view content vs displayed rows.
- `:append-to PATH` — appends marked lines to file (existing content preserved).
- `:write-to -` on log view writes each line + `\n` to stdout.

## 6. :goto / navigation

`:goto N` (0-based line number), `N%`, ISO timestamp, or `#anchor`. No output on success;
it moves the top-of-view, so the exit dump starts at that line.
- `:goto 3` on 8-line file → dump starts at 4th line. `:goto 50%` → starts at line idx 4.
- `:goto 2024-01-15T10:00:06` → dump starts at the line with that timestamp.
- `:goto abc` → error box `invalid argument: abc` /
  `reason: expecting line number/percentage, timestamp, or relative time`.
- `:head`, `:tail`, `:pwd` DO NOT EXIST → `error: unknown command: ‘head’` etc.
  (`:head` gets a "did you mean" note, `:tail`/`:pwd` don't.)
- `:echoln` DOES NOT EXIST as a command (echoln() is an SQL function only).

## 7. :comment / :tag / :annotate / :partition-name

- Attach to the focused line (use `:goto 0` first). No direct output.
- They DO affect the exit dump: the line is followed by metadata lines:
  ```
  2024-01-15T10:00:01.000 INFO starting up service alpha
  └ Line 0 metadata
   ┴ #BUG123 #review
  ```
  (`└` = U+2514, `┴` = U+2534; one leading space before `┴`.)
  `:comment this is my comment` renders identically with the comment text after `┴ `.
  Markdown is rendered/stripped in the dump: `**markdown**` → `markdown`.
  (Comments/tags do NOT appear in `:write-view-to` output, only in the exit dump.)
- `:tag` with no args → `error: expecting one or more tags`; tag without `#` prefix
  accepted silently.
- `:comment` with no text → error box `expecting some comment text`.
- `:annotate` on a plain log line → error box `no annotations available for this log message`.
- `:partition-name boot1` → no output, no error.

## 8. :highlight

- `:highlight ERROR` — no output, no error, and NO visible effect on headless output
  (no ANSI color codes added to the dump).
- Bad regex (`:highlight [`) → same regex error box as `:filter-in [`.

## 9. :cd / :sh / :redirect-to

- `:cd DIR` — silent on success; affects subsequent `:sh` cwd. Missing dir → error box
  `cannot access -- <dir>` / `reason: No such file or directory`. No `:pwd` command.
- `:sh CMDLINE` — runs via the shell (looks like `/bin/bash -c`): `;`, `>&2` work.
  Child's stdout AND stderr are both captured to lnav's stdout, in order
  (`:sh echo out; echo err >&2` → stdout: `out\nerr\n`).
  Child failure: `:sh nosuchcmd123` → stdout `/bin/bash: line 1: nosuchcmd123: command not found`;
  `:sh exit 3` → no output; lnav exit code stays 0 in all cases.
  `--name=<name>` option exists (per help) but was not needed for output capture.
- `:redirect-to PATH` — redirects output of commands that write to stdout
  (`:echo` verified; both echos appended to the file, one line each). `:redirect-to`
  with no arg clears the redirect. The SQL-result exit dump is NOT redirected (still
  stdout). Unwritable path → error box `unable to open file -- <path>`, and the
  following `:echo` still goes to stdout.
- `:open PATH` from `-c`: missing file → `error: cannot open file: <path>` + reason
  (exit 0, unlike CLI-arg files which exit 1).

## 10. Time commands

- `:current-time` → `Sat Aug 08 20:39:36 2026  +0000 UTC -- 1786221576`
  (format: `%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y` + two spaces + numeric tz offset + ` UTC -- ` + epoch).
- `:unix-time 1490191111` → `Wed Mar 22 13:58:31 2017  +0000 UTC -- 1490191111`.
  No arg → error box `expecting a unix time value`.
- `:convert-time-to ZONE` — operates on focused log line; fails in this container
  (`discover_tz_dir failed to find zoneinfo`), so full behavior unverified here.
- `:set-file-timezone ZONE [pattern]` / `:clear-file-timezone` — no output, no error.

## 11. Misc notes

- SQL (`;`) results are only visible via the exit dump, `:write-screen-to/table-to/...`
  or are lost when a later command writes to stdout.
- The `= help:` box always shows the command's signature and its 1–2 line description
  from the Command Reference, wrapped with 10-space indent.
- `:switch-to-view log` after a `;SELECT` makes the exit dump show the log view again.
- `:highlight-field`, `:spectrogram`, `:summarize`, `:prompt`, `:export-session-to`,
  `:session`, `:pipe-to`, `:pipe-line-to`, breakpoints, sticky headers: not tested
  (lower priority / interactive-oriented).

Spec written to `/tmp/t/cmds/NOTES.md` (288 lines). Summary of findings:

## Global headless behavior (the big discoveries)

- **Exit dump**: with stdout piped and no `-q`, lnav prints the top view (filtered, from current top line to EOF) to stdout at exit. After a `;SELECT` the top view is the DB result (plain aligned columns). **The dump is suppressed if any `-c` command already wrote to stdout** (`:echo`, `:write-*-to -`, `:sh`).
- **`-q`** suppresses only the exit dump, not `:echo`.
- **Errors always go to stderr, exit code stays 0**, and later `-c` commands still run. Exit 1 only for an unopenable CLI-arg file (`error: unable to open file: ...` + `reason: No such file or directory`).

## Command highlights

- **`:echo`**: message after the first separating space is verbatim (spaces, quotes, `;` preserved; quotes NOT stripped). `$VAR`/`${VAR}` env-substituted (undefined → empty), `\$` escapes; `\t`/`\n` are *not* escapes (`\t` → `t`). `-n` omits newline. Output → stdout.
- **`:eval`**: runs a command/query after env substitution — `:eval ;SELECT 1+1` and `:eval :echo ...` work; `:eval 1+1` → `unknown command: ‘1+1’` with full help box.
- **`:filter-in`/`:filter-out`**: change the dump/`write-*` contents; filters AND together; duplicates silently idempotent; no file → silent success.
- **`write-*`**: `-` = stdout. File writes are **silent** (no "wrote N rows") and silently overwrite. `:write-to`/`:write-raw-to` require marked lines (`error: no lines marked to write, use 'm' to mark lines`; use `:mark-expr 1`). `:write-jsonlines-to --all` needs no marks. Formats captured exactly: CSV (header row), pretty JSON (4-space indent), JSON Lines (compact), json-cols (odd leading-comma style), table (Unicode box + ANSI bold even to files/pipes), screen (plain 10-wide columns, trailing space).
- **`:goto`** takes 0-based line / `N%` / timestamp; moves dump start. **`:head`, `:tail`, `:pwd`, `:echoln` don't exist** → `error: unknown command: ‘head’` (head gets a "did you mean" note).
- **`:comment`/`:tag`**: render in the exit dump as `└ Line 0 metadata` + ` ┴ <text>` lines (markdown stripped), but not in `:write-view-to`. No-arg errors: `expecting some comment text` / `expecting one or more tags`. `:annotate` → `no annotations available for this log message`.
- **`:highlight`**: zero effect on headless output; bad regex gives the standard regex error box.
- **`:sh`**: runs via `/bin/bash -c`; child stdout *and* stderr both captured to lnav stdout; child exit code ignored (lnav stays 0). `:cd` affects it; bad `:cd` → `cannot access -- <dir>` box. **`:redirect-to`** captures `:echo` output to a file but not the exit dump.
- **`:current-time`/`:unix-time`**: `Wed Mar 22 13:58:31 2017  +0000 UTC -- 1490191111` format. `:convert-time-to` fails in this container (no zoneinfo).

## Error format (all stderr)

- Unknown command: single line `  error: unknown command: ‘name’` (curly quotes U+2018/19), optional `= note: did you mean...` list.
- Arg errors: box of `  error:` / ` reason:` / ` --> command-option:N` (1-based `-c` index) / ` | <original command>` (space-padded to ≥43 cols) / ` = help: <signature>` / 71×`═` / indented description. Bad regex uses ` --> pattern` with a ` ^ <pcre error>` caret line, block padded to its longest line.

Not tested (low priority/interactive): `:prompt`, `:spectrogram`, `:export-session-to`, `:pipe-to`, breakpoints, sticky headers. All commands, exact bytes (cat -A), and untested items are documented in `/tmp/t/cmds/NOTES.md`.
